_comment: Manual relevance judgments for each query. 'relevant' lists the IDs of documents judged as relevant by the group. 'retrieved' lists the IDs actually returned by buscar() in rank order.

queries.notes: Only docs 2 and 8 spell out 'inteligência artificial' in full. Docs 6, 7, 9, 10 use the acronym 'IA', so the FTS query does not match them — classic synonym/abbreviation limitation.
Doc 3 contains 'bancos' but never 'dados'; doc 4 contains 'dados' but never 'banco'. Both miss the AND requirement of the tsquery, so they are not retrieved despite being relevant.
Perfect match — only doc 1 mentions PostgreSQL.
In Portuguese FTS, 'ia' is a stop word (past imperfect of 'ir'). websearch_to_tsquery returns an empty tsquery, so no documents are retrieved. This illustrates the stop-word/acronym limitation.
Doc 10 is thematically relevant (AI improves medical precision/performance) but uses 'precisão', not 'desempenho', so it is not retrieved.
Doc 5 is about data protection and security but uses 'criptografia', 'controle de acesso', 'auditoria' — never the stem of 'segurança' — so it is missed.
Both docs match perfectly. Doc 9 ranks higher because 'Regulamentação' appears in its title (weight A).
Perfect match — only doc 4 mentions 'machine learning'.
Doc 8 ('análise de dados') is retrieved but is not a database document — false positive. Doc 3 (MongoDB) is relevant but never uses 'dados' in its text — false negative.
